hero.subheadline: Three cash prizes totaling $1,700 for photography that explores life
hero.valueProposition: Amateur and professional photographers worldwide can win up to $1,000 by submitting original images on the theme Recurring Patterns in Life.

content.whyJoin:
Philo-Photo is an annual photography contest organized by New Acropolis that pairs photography with philosophy, inviting images that spark curiosity and reflection. The 2026 theme is Recurring Patterns in Life (Nature and Humanity), and the contest accepts original photographs taken with a camera or smartphone.

The contest offers $1,700 in cash awards across three places: $1,000 for the overall winner, $500 for second place, and $200 for third place. All winners receive downloadable certificates and an online gallery showcase, and the top winner earns the honorary title of Photographer of the Year.

Because it is open to both amateur and professional photographers aged 18 and above from around the world, and each photographer may submit up to three images, Philo-Photo is an accessible entry point for photographers who want their work seen within a themed, idea-driven community.
content.whoShouldApply:
This contest is for photographers aged 18 and above at any experience level, from amateurs to professionals, who want to interpret a philosophical theme through their images. It suits photographers who work with a camera or smartphone and can produce original, unmanipulated photographs.

The annual theme invites a wide range of responses, so both new photographers submitting a single strong image and experienced photographers submitting the full three are welcome. Organizers and judges cannot participate, but all other photographers worldwide are eligible.

faq.question: Who can enter the Philo-Photo contest?
faq.answer: The contest is open to both amateur and professional photographers from around the world who are 18 years old or older. Organizers and judges are not allowed to participate, and each photographer may submit up to three single images related to the annual theme.

faq.question: What kinds of photos are accepted?
faq.answer: The contest accepts original photographs created using photographic techniques, including images taken with a camera or smartphone. Entries are not eligible if they were created with generative AI tools or Photoshop, or if they include watermarks, explicit or violent content, wildlife harassment, environmental damage, or people photographed without required consent.

faq.question: What are the file requirements for submission?
faq.answer: Images must be submitted as JPG files in sRGB or Adobe98, 8-bit, with the longest side at 1100 pixels and a maximum file size of 1.5 MB. Images must not include borders, logos, or watermarks. Winners must be able to provide a high-resolution version and may be asked for the original RAW file to verify ownership.

faq.question: How much does it cost to enter?
faq.answer: The entry fee is $22 for one photo, $38 for two photos, or $45 for three photos. The contest awards $1,000 for first place, $500 for second place, and $200 for third place, with winners also receiving certificates and online gallery exposure.

faq.question: What is the theme for the 2026 edition?
faq.answer: The 2026 theme is Recurring Patterns in Life (Nature and Humanity). Entries are expected to relate to the annual theme, and the contest is described as a space where philosophy and photography meet.

submissionGuide.detail: Create an account at philophoto.org by signing up via the register page. Registration is required before submitting entries.

Select up to three original photographs that relate to the 2026 theme Recurring Patterns in Life. Convert them to JPG in sRGB or Adobe98, 8-bit, with the longest side at 1100 pixels and a maximum file size of 1.5 MB, without borders, logos, or watermarks.

submissionGuide.step: Submit and pay the entry fee
submissionGuide.detail: Upload your images and pay the entry fee of $22 for one photo, $38 for two photos, or $45 for three photos. The fee covers your submission.

The contest awards $1,000 for first place, $500 for second, and $200 for third. Winners receive certificates and an online gallery showcase, and selected winners may need to provide high-resolution or original RAW files for verification.
